The Lotus Evora family

7 generations and variants in the Index, 2009–2021. Oldest first; every card opens the full page, with its own versions, figures and story.

  1. 2009–2014

    Lotus Evora

    Lotus's bid to build a grown-up car that still felt like a Lotus: a mid-engined 2+2 grand tourer with room for luggage, real comfort and a Toyota V6, and the first of a line Lotus built at Hethel until 2021. The line survived its maker's near-collapse, improved almost every year, and earned a reputation for some of the finest steering and ride quality of its era.

    276 hp4.9 sec 0-60162 mph top6,117 built
  2. 2010–2014

    Lotus Evora S

    The Evora with a supercharger. For 2010 Lotus took the Toyota V6 from 276 hp to 345 hp and gave the S revised suspension, larger brakes and a rear spoiler of its own, and it was the quick Evora until the 400 replaced it in 2015.

    345 hp4.6 sec 0-60172 mph top6,117 built
  3. 2015–2021

    Lotus Evora 400

    The Evora reworked into something harder and faster. Lotus said more than two-thirds of it was new, the supercharged V6 rose to 400 hp, a limited-slip differential came standard with the manual, and it was the most powerful production Lotus yet when it arrived in 2015.

    400 hp4.1 sec 0-60186 mph top6,117 built
  4. 2016–2021

    Lotus Evora Sport 410

    The lighter, sharper Evora. Unveiled at Geneva in 2016 with carbon-fiber body parts and 410 hp, it became the GT410 Sport for Lotus's 70th anniversary and later the softer GT410, the forms in which the 410 hp Evora ran to the end.

    410 hp3.9 sec 0-60190 mph top6,117 built
  5. 2017–2018

    Lotus Evora GT430

    The most extreme Evora. Lotus planned just 60, gave them 430 hp, a dry weight of 1,258 kg and bodywork that could make up to 250 kg of downforce, and called it the most powerful road car it had built to that point.

    430 hp3.7 sec 0-60190 mph top60 built
  6. 2017–2018

    Lotus Evora GT430 Sport

    The GT430 without the wing. Lotus took off the big rear wing to cut drag, kept the 430 hp V6, quoted a dry weight of 1,248 kg and 196 mph, and called it the fastest production Lotus yet.

    430 hp3.7 sec 0-60196 mph top6,117 built
  7. 2020–2021

    Lotus Evora GT

    The Evora's North American farewell: a supercharged, mid-engined 2+2 with 416 hp, a clutch pedal and hydraulic steering, sold for just 2 model years before the Emira took over. It tied a Porsche 911 GT3 to 60 mph in testing, but its real case rests on how it feels on a good road.

    416 hp4.0 sec 0-60188 mph top6,117 built
